hints.title: What do you need to remember?
hints.body: As you scan the list, what information about the values you have already seen would let you answer immediately for the current value?

hints.title: Look for the complement
hints.body: For a value `x`, the value you need is `target - x`. A hash map from a value to its index can tell you whether that complement has already appeared.

hints.title: One pass, check before inserting
hints.body: Walk through the list once. For each index `i`, check whether `target - nums[i]` is already in the map. If it is, return the stored index and `i`. Otherwise store `nums[i] -> i`. Check before inserting so one element cannot pair with itself.

hints.title: Pseudocode
hints.body:
```
seen = empty map
for i from 0 to length(nums) - 1:
    complement = target - nums[i]
    if complement is in seen:
        return [seen[complement], i]
    seen[nums[i]] = i
return empty list
```

This is pseudocode, not a complete solution. Translate it into your language and test it against the examples.
